subject.title: refactor(meeting-bot): extract browser meeting-bot core behind MeetingPlatformAdapter

question: Should OpenClaw publish the current 81-export `meeting-runtime` plugin API now, or narrow/internalize the contract until the planned second platform proves the reusable boundary?
rationale: The branch is technically plausible, but a new public plugin SDK subpath is a lasting compatibility commitment whose appropriate breadth cannot be settled by tests or automated review alone.

options.title: Narrow the public contract first
options.body: Keep the core extraction but expose only the smallest adapter/runtime surface required by Google Meet and the next concrete platform before committing the broader helpers publicly.

options.title: Approve the current SDK surface
options.body: Accept the 81-export contract as the supported meeting-plugin API and require compatibility documentation, focused API tests, and live upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Pause for the Teams adapter
options.body: Hold this PR until the planned Teams implementation demonstrates the abstraction and identifies which exports are genuinely shared.

recommendation.title: Narrow the public contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the core extraction but expose only the smallest adapter/runtime surface required by Google Meet and the next concrete platform before committing the broader helpers publicly.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the preceding merged consolidation layers and has the clearest available context for the intended meeting-platform architecture.
